process: 3 independent seats (deep-reasoner, codex, skill-creator-audit) -> per-finding adversarial verify

seats.verdict: Solid, well-tested harness whose docs are mostly faithful to the code — the load-bearing safety claims (fail-closed exit matrix, the four validation refusals, untracked-file reviewer diff, setup-config/gitignore behavior, artifact list, every-profile validation) all check out against the source and live runs. One genuine doc-to-behavior break undermines trust: `final_reviewer` is shipped in the default config and described as a gated role but is never invoked, so a user who configures it gets a silent no-op. Beyond that, the Workflow section is not self-contained for full mode or a cold start, and a handful of minor factual drifts remain. Fix the final_reviewer contradiction and round out the Workflow; the rest is polish. As a security audit was explicitly out of scope, this review only covers documentation-to-behavior parity and operating-agent UX."
strengths: Exit-code contract is exact and fail-closed: fullModeProblems (agent-council.mjs:309-340) and reportRunOutcome (288-303) implement precisely the 0/1 matrix SKILL.md:55-59 and architecture.md:161 describe (builder complete + proof exit 0 + APPROVED = 0; killed/blocked builder, failed/timed-out proof, REVISE/UNKNOWN = 1), and SIGINT/SIGTERM map to 130/143 (1290-1315). Do not loosen.

All four validation refusals in SKILL.md:45 are enforced by reference-identity checks: duplicate advisors (677), write_mode advisor/final_reviewer (683/688 via assertReadOnlySeat 801-805), builder==reviewer (705), builder write_mode (709), reviewer non-write (713), resume_command --last/{thread_id} (745-751).

The prior-review P1 fix is present and correct: the reviewer diff includes untracked new files via `git diff --no-index` and excludes the council's own artifacts from both tracked and untracked sections (gitDiffForReview 2430-2447, untrackedDiff 2457-2489); git failures surface inline rather than as an empty diff (section 2449-2455).

--print-sample-config emits a config byte-identical to references/sample-config.yaml (live-verified), and setup-config writes exactly `.agents/agent-council.yaml` plus a `.agent-council/` .gitignore entry as SKILL.md:28 promises (live-verified in a temp git repo).

Artifact filename list in SKILL.md:83-92 matches the code exactly (task.md 218, config.resolved.json 219, council.initial.json 2331, self-grill-<n>.json/adversarial-<n>.json 878/903 via artifactName, parent-synthesis-prompt.md 257, build-report.json 998).

--validate-config genuinely checks every profile, not just the selected one (validateEveryProfile 652-666), honoring SKILL.md:37-38; covered by a dedicated test. Full deterministic suite is green (35 tests).
top_improvements: Resolve the final_reviewer contradiction (P1): make the seat actually run a closing review in soft/hard mode, or strip it from both sample configs and the SKILL.md:45 guard so the shipped starter config makes no promise the runner silently ignores.

Make the Workflow self-contained for the two hard cases it currently skips: a full-mode command template with --allow-writes and --proof-cmd, and a cold-start 'no config yet -> --setup-config -> edit' step, so a fresh agent completes both loops without hitting an error and back-tracking into the Required Config / Modes prose.

Correct the small factual drifts (setup-config 'always .agents/...' path, the preset parenthetical that miscounts advisors, the architecture git-diff --cached mechanism, and the bare $ARGUMENTS footgun) — each is a place where an operator who trusts the doc verbatim gets a mild surprise.

findings.claim: The `final_reviewer` seat is shipped in the default soft/hard profiles and is described in SKILL.md as a real gated role, but the runner never invokes it — it is inert. A user who follows the docs and assigns a reviewer seat gets no final-review pass and no warning.
findings.evidence: references/sample-config.yaml:8 and :16 set `final_reviewer: claude-opus`; SKILL.md:45 lists it as a guarded role ('a write_mode seat listed as an advisor or final reviewer'). In scripts/agent-council.mjs `final_reviewer` appears ONLY at 686-688 (validation) and 783 (normalizeProfile); an exhaustive grep of the single-file script and both test files shows no consumer that runs it. Soft/hard runs proceed with the parent as sole synthesizer, so the seat does nothing.
findings.fix: Either wire `final_reviewer` into soft/hard mode (run it as a distinct closing review pass and surface its output), or remove it from both sample configs, drop the SKILL.md:45 guard reference, and delete the dead validate/normalize branches so the shipped config makes no promise the runner won't keep.

verify.reasoning: Factual core CONFIRMED by independent read: references/sample-config.yaml:8 and :16 ship `final_reviewer: claude-opus` in the default soft/hard profiles (and the embedded SAMPLE_CONFIG at scripts/agent-council.mjs:40/48 — what --setup-config actually writes — matches). SKILL.md:45 and glossary.md:31 describe it as a write-gate-guarded role. In the 73KB runner, `final_reviewer` appears only in validation (686-688) and normalizeProfile (783); the run flow (initial council → self-grill/adversarial → full-mode build) never invokes it — the full-mode review at line 1055 uses the separate `profile.reviewer` field. Neither test file mentions it. architecture.md:197 lists "richer final reviewer contracts" only as future Scaling Direction; nothing marks the field intentionally inert and no warning is emitted. The seat is dead config, and the proposed fix (wire or remove) is correct. However, P1 is inflated: SKILL.md's Modes section never promises a final-review pass in soft/hard ("run configured advisors once and produce a parent synthesis prompt"), so no documented behavior breaks; no wrong output is produced; the vacuous write_mode guard fails safe (it rejects, never permits). The defect is a silently ignored config knob in shipped defaults that can mislead an operator into believing an extra review pass ran — real doc/config-integrity debt (and against the repo's own "never a hidden flag" convention), but quality-tier, not a broken critical path. Severity corrected to P2.

findings.claim: The Workflow section gives only a hard-mode command template; there is no runnable full-mode example anywhere in SKILL.md, and no cold-start step for the missing-config case. A fresh agent told to run a full council must assemble `--allow-writes` and a mandatory `--proof-cmd <cmd>` from Modes prose, guessing the proof command.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:67-72 is the only command block and uses `--profile hard` with no write/proof flags; SKILL.md:51 states full mode 'Requires --allow-writes, a clean git tree, and --proof-cmd' only in prose; the Workflow (61-79) never links back to Required Config (22-45), so following it top-to-bottom with no config hits the runner's 'Config required... Run with --setup-config' error at step 3 before any council runs.
findings.fix: Add a full-mode command template to the Workflow (with `--allow-writes --proof-cmd '<repo gate>'`) and a leading step 0: 'if no config exists, run --setup-config and edit it (see Required Config)'.

verify.reasoning: Facts at the cited locations are accurate: SKILL.md:67-72 is the only council-invocation command block (hard mode, no write/proof flags); full-mode requirements exist only as prose at SKILL.md:51; the Workflow list has no config-bootstrap step; the runner's missing-config error (agent-council.mjs:542) matches the quote. But three details/severity points are off. (1) "--proof-cmd" is not mandatory: SKILL.md:51 and buildProofCommand (agent-council.mjs:2348) accept profile.proof_cmd — though the shipped sample-config full profile omits it, so the flag is practically needed with the starter config. (2) The failure modes are all fail-fast, pre-spend, and self-healing: missing config errors at loadConfig before any child CLI spawns and names the recovery (--setup-config); missing full-mode flags error at assertBuildAllowed (main line 198) BEFORE the initial council phase, with exact-flag messages ("pass --allow-writes explicitly", "Full mode requires --proof-cmd or profile.proof_cmd") — so no paid sessions are wasted, contrary to the finding's implied cost. (3) "Never links back to Required Config" ignores that Required Config is a top-level section 40 lines above Workflow in the same 111-line file, giving the exact --setup-config command; the flags are also in --help usage. Under the package's declared threat model (workflow harness, trusted operator config), this is a docs-ergonomics polish gap — one instant retry on a self-describing error — not P2. The proposed fix (full-mode template + step 0) is still worthwhile and cheap.

findings.claim: SKILL.md states `--setup-config` 'always writes .agents/agent-council.yaml into the current repo'. It does not when `--config <other>` or `AGENT_COUNCIL_CONFIG` is set; the target is `resolve(cwd, options.configPath)`.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:28 ('always writes `.agents/agent-council.yaml`'); scripts/agent-council.mjs:554 `const targetPath = resolve(options.cwd, options.configPath)` where options.configPath defaults to AGENT_COUNCIL_CONFIG || DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH (line 355) and is overridden by `--config` (401-402).
findings.fix: Change 'always writes .agents/agent-council.yaml' to 'writes to the --config path (default .agents/agent-council.yaml)'.

verify.reasoning: Every cited fact checks out in the source. SKILL.md:27-28 states --setup-config 'always writes .agents/agent-council.yaml into the current repo'. The code contradicts this: writeSetupConfig (agent-council.mjs:554) targets resolve(options.cwd, options.configPath); configPath defaults to AGENT_COUNCIL_CONFIG || '.agents/agent-council.yaml' (line 355) and is overridden by --config (lines 401-402); args are fully parsed before the setupConfig dispatch (line 172), so --config always flows into the setup write regardless of flag order. The script's OWN --help (line 142) even says '--setup-config: Write a recommended config to --config path and exit', so SKILL.md contradicts the tool's built-in usage text — an internal doc inconsistency. Also, --cwd (lines 406-408) can redirect 'the current repo' part, same class of inaccuracy not mentioned by the reviewer. At the declared threat model (workflow harness, trusted operator config) this is a pure documentation-accuracy defect, not security: an operator with AGENT_COUNCIL_CONFIG exported would get the config written to an unexpected path while SKILL.md promises otherwise. P3 is the correct, non-inflated tier, and the proposed fix wording matches the CLI's own help text.

findings.claim: The inline comment 'opencode preset: Codex + Claude Code seats, OpenCode advisors' mischaracterizes the shipped config: all four seats (codex-readonly, claude-opus, deepseek-pro, glm) are advisors in every profile, not just the two OpenCode seats.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:31 parenthetical; references/sample-config.yaml:7, :13, :21 list all four as `advisors`.
findings.fix: Reword to 'four advisor seats: Codex, Claude Code, and two OpenCode Go models' to match the config.

verify.reasoning: Core claim verified: all four seats (codex-readonly, claude-opus, deepseek-pro, glm) are advisors in every profile — confirmed in references/sample-config.yaml:7,:13,:21 AND in the byte-identical SAMPLE_CONFIG inside scripts/agent-council.mjs (:39,:45,:53), which is what --setup-config writes; the 'opencode preset' name is real (agent-council.mjs:143,:602-607). The parenthetical's natural reading (advisors = OpenCode only) does mislead about which paid sessions a soft/hard run spawns. Two details are off, blocking CONFIRMED: (1) 'mischaracterizes' overstates — the preset ships SIX seats, and 'Codex + Claude Code seats' has a defensible compressed reading: those providers fill multiple seats (advisor plus codex-builder/claude-reviewer at sample-config.yaml:52-64) while OpenCode models are advisor-only; the comment is ambiguous, not flatly false. (2) The proposed fix is itself inaccurate-by-omission: 'four advisor seats: Codex, Claude Code, and two OpenCode Go models' describes only 4 of the 6 shipped seats, dropping the builder/reviewer seats the original comment was plausibly compressing; a correct reword must mention both, e.g. 'four advisors (Codex, Claude Code, two OpenCode Go models) plus Codex builder / Claude reviewer seats for full mode'. Severity P3 fits the declared threat model (doc-clarity nit, trusted operator config) — not inflated, stays P3.

findings.claim: Architecture says the reviewer diff is 'git diff HEAD (or git diff plus git diff --cached before the first commit)'. The code instead diffs against a fixed baseline SHA (HEAD or the empty-tree SHA), never running a separate `git diff --cached`. The result is equivalent but the described mechanism is wrong.
findings.evidence: references/architecture.md:165; scripts/agent-council.mjs:2431 `base = baseline || captureReviewBaseline(cwd)` (2422-2424 returns HEAD sha or EMPTY_TREE_SHA), 2439/2441 run `git diff <base> ...` — no `--cached` invocation.
findings.fix: Describe it as 'git diff against HEAD, or against the empty-tree object before the first commit, supplemented by a --no-index diff of untracked files'.

verify.reasoning:
Core claim verified against the sources. references/architecture.md:165 says the reviewer diff is built from "`git diff HEAD` (or `git diff` plus `git diff --cached` before the first commit)". The code does neither: scripts/agent-council.mjs:2422-2425 (captureReviewBaseline) resolves a fixed SHA — HEAD via rev-parse, or EMPTY_TREE_SHA (4b825dc6...) in a repo with no commits — and gitDiffForReview (2430-2448) runs `git diff <base> --stat` and `git diff <base>` against that SHA. `grep -n "cached"` over the whole 73K script returns nothing; no `git diff --cached` is ever invoked. The doc-code mismatch is real, and architecture.md:165 is the only doc making the claim.

Two details of the finding are off, which is why PARTIAL rather than CONFIRMED:

1. "The result is equivalent but the described mechanism is wrong" — the result is NOT equivalent. The baseline is pinned BEFORE the builder runs (agent-council.mjs:923-931, comment: "a builder that commits its work is still diffed, not just one that leaves a dirty worktree"). A live `git diff HEAD` at review time, as documented, would silently drop everything the builder committed; the pinned-baseline diff catches unstaged, staged, and committed changes (comment at 2427-2429). So the doc is behaviorally misleading, not just mechanically mislabeled — the finding slightly understates the discrepancy.

2. The proposed fix repeats the same error: "git diff against HEAD, or against the empty-tree object before the first commit" omits the pinning, which the code treats as load-bearing. Correct wording: "git diff against a baseline SHA pinned before the builder runs — HEAD at that moment, or the empty-tree object in a repo with no commits — supplemented by a --no-index diff of untracked files, with the council's artifacts directory excluded from both."

Severity P3 stands: a doc-accuracy defect in a reference file, no code change needed, consistent with the ADR-0001 threat model (workflow harness, trusted operator input). No inflation to correct.

findings.claim: The Workflow command ends with `-- "$ARGUMENTS"`. Run verbatim in bash, `$ARGUMENTS` is an unset env var expanding to an empty string, so a literal copy-paste launches the council with an empty task.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:71 `-- "$ARGUMENTS"`; the runner accepts an empty trailing task and would proceed.
findings.fix: Note explicitly that `$ARGUMENTS` is a placeholder to replace with the restated task text, or use an angle-bracket placeholder like `-- "<task>"` to signal substitution.

verify.reasoning: The cited text exists (SKILL.md:71 ends with `-- "$ARGUMENTS"`), but the finding's load-bearing evidence — "the runner accepts an empty trailing task and would proceed" — is factually false. In scripts/agent-council.mjs, parseArgs joins and trims everything after `--` (line 509: `options.prompt = promptParts.join(" ").trim()`), so an unset `$ARGUMENTS` yields an empty prompt; main() then falls back to stdin (line 191) and, if that is also empty, throws before any artifact write or seat spawn (line 194: "No council task provided. Pass it after -- or pipe it on stdin."). Verified empirically: running the command verbatim with ARGUMENTS unset and stdin closed (a valid sample config supplied) exits 1 with exactly that message — no council launches, no paid CLI sessions spawn. In an interactive TTY the process would block awaiting stdin EOF instead; still no empty-task run. So the claimed failure scenario cannot occur; the runner already fails closed. Additionally, `$ARGUMENTS` is the standard Claude Code slash-command/skill substitution token: in the skill's own primary invocation path (user-invoked `/agent-council <task>`, per frontmatter `disable-model-invocation: true`), the harness substitutes the user's text into the body before the model executes anything, so the placeholder is intentional convention, not an oversight — and the proposed `<task>` angle-bracket fix would break that substitution path. At the declared threat model (workflow harness, trusted operator), a naive copy-paste producing a clear, self-explanatory error is immaterial.

seats.verdict: Solid safety/trust design and clear operating instructions, but two doc paths actively mislead a careful follower (silent-typo validation, broken example commands), and the starter config ships an inert field, an understated cost model, and a timeout contradicted by the package's own evidence. Independent Codex review confirms these are real, current findings against the code — not overlap with the earlier fixed P1/P2 items.
strengths: Concise sequenced workflow in SKILL.md with an explicit completion criterion (must account for every configured seat result).

Candid trust model: child output is advisory-only, hostile-repo risk and adapter permissions are called out explicitly, OpenCode recursion/permission handling documented (references/architecture.md:89-105).
Full mode has clean fail-closed semantics: proof failure, incomplete builder, non-approval verdict all block success (SKILL.md:51-59; ADR 0002).
Explicitly documents Claude Code's skill-discovery paths and the required install symlink instead of pretending .agents/skills alone is sufficient (references/architecture.md:202-225).
Glossary cleanly distinguishes per-seat timeout vs. whole-council deadline vs. failure vs. unreadable verdict.

Test suite covers meaningful behavior (full-mode proof/review, untracked files, process failure, timeouts, recursion refusal, config validation, output containment); count growth from 14→33 checks out against current file.
top_improvements: Close the config schema (reject unknown/misspelled keys) and either wire up or delete `final_reviewer` — right now "validated" config can silently diverge from what runs.
Fix path-relative doc commands in `references/architecture.md` so they work from the documented invocation context.
Replace the vague cost warning with an explicit call-count model and recalibrate starter defaults (profile choice + Claude timeout) to match already-observed behavior.

findings.claim: SKILL.md's validate step is not schema-closed. Profile and seat validators inspect recognized properties without rejecting unknown ones, then normalization silently substitutes defaults. A typo (e.g. `self_gril_rounds`, `timeout_m`) gets "config ok" while silently changing council rigor/duration.
findings.fix: Enforce allowed-key allowlists at root/profile/seat levels, reject unknown keys with full path + nearest-name suggestion, add regression tests for misspelled round/timeout/prompt-mode/full-mode fields.

verify.reasoning:
The factual core is accurate and I reproduced it from the code. Validation is not schema-closed at any level: resolveConfig (agent-council.mjs:610-648) checks only version/profiles/seats/default_profile and ignores other root keys; validateProfile (:668-718) and validateSeat (:720-775) inspect recognized keys only and never reject unknown ones (the only "Unknown" errors in the file are for CLI flags at :503 and setup presets at :607). normalizeProfile (:777-791) then substitutes silent defaults: a typo'd `self_gril_rounds` in a hard profile yields `self_grill_rounds ?? 0`, and the phase loops at :871/:896 run zero self-grill/adversarial rounds; a seat `timeout_m` typo yields `timeout_ms: 0` (:772), which falls back to the global default at :1102/:1122. Meanwhile `--validate-config` prints "agent-council config ok" (:181-186). No test in agent-council.test.mjs or agent-council.e2e.test.mjs covers unknown/misspelled keys, and neither SKILL.md:43-45 nor the ADRs document unknown-key tolerance as intended. So the defect is real and material even under the declared threat model (docs/adr/0001: workflow harness, trusted operator config): SKILL.md:37-38 explicitly sells `--validate-config` as the post-edit check, and it green-lights a config that silently degrades the product's core deliverable (review rigor) and wastes paid CLI runs.

What's off is the severity. P1 overstates it because every safety-relevant field fails CLOSED under a key typo, which the finding does not acknowledge: `write_mode` defaults to false, so a typo can never silently grant writes — a full-mode builder with a typo'd `write_mode` key fails validation loudly at :709-711; a typo'd `proof_cmd` normalizes to "" and full mode then throws in assertBuildAllowed (:815-825); typo'd builder/reviewer/advisor seat references throw via requireSeat (:793-797). The silent-degradation direction only ever reduces rounds or shifts timeouts toward defaults — it cannot escalate privilege, corrupt anything, or bypass the write gates. Additionally the degradation is observable after the fact: the run's Phase Summary and artifacts (self-grill-<n>.json / adversarial-<n>.json simply absent) reflect the actual rounds executed, and SKILL.md's workflow requires the parent to account for every phase row. A trusted-operator footgun that is fail-safe on all write paths and visible in run output is a P2 robustness/UX defect, not P1. The proposed fix (allowlists at root/profile/seat with path + nearest-name suggestion, plus regression tests) is proportionate and correct.

findings.claim: `references/architecture.md` gives `node scripts/...` examples (smoke test, SDK check, deterministic tests) that assume CWD = skill directory, but the package elsewhere establishes commands run from the adopting repo root — where that path doesn't exist.
findings.fix: Use install-root-qualified paths (`.agents/skills/agent-council/scripts/...`) consistently, or prefix examples with an explicit `cd`.

verify.reasoning: Core claim verified by direct read. architecture.md:147, :172 (node scripts/agent-council.mjs), :181 (node scripts/claude-agent-sdk-adapter.mjs --help), and :187-188 (node --test scripts/agent-council.*.mjs) use bare scripts/... paths that resolve only with CWD = skill directory. SKILL.md:24-28 explicitly establishes the opposite convention ("Paths resolve against the CURRENT working directory", commands assume the project-local install root) and every SKILL.md command — including the identical test commands at SKILL.md:100-101 — uses the qualified .agents/skills/agent-council/scripts/... spelling. architecture.md is even internally inconsistent: line 75 uses the qualified spelling for the SDK adapter seat. A package-wide grep found no doc establishing a skill-dir CWD context, so nothing rescues the bare paths; the bare spelling additionally escapes the allowed-tools rule Bash(node .agents/skills/agent-council/scripts/agent-council.mjs:*), and sources.md:35 repeats the same defect (unreported). What's off: (1) the :107-109 citation is prose about the sample config's location, not a runnable command — the real evidence is 144-189; (2) P1 is inflated for the declared threat model (workflow harness, trusted operator, no security boundary): the failure is loud and immediate (Cannot find module), lives in a secondary reference doc while the primary operative doc is correct, and self-corrects in one step — a real doc defect worth fixing, not a major functional or gate-defeating problem. Proposed fix is correct and matches the package's own convention.

findings.claim: `sample-config.yaml` sets `final_reviewer` on soft/hard profiles, implying a final review/synthesis pass. The harness only checks the seat exists and is read-only, then never invokes it — execution goes straight from grill/adversarial rounds to build/parent synthesis.
findings.fix: Either implement a real final-review phase with documented authority, or remove `final_reviewer` from schema/starter config.

verify.reasoning: Every factual element checks out. sample-config.yaml lines 8/16 and the embedded SAMPLE_CONFIG (agent-council.mjs lines 40/48, written by --setup-config) set final_reviewer on soft and hard profiles. A whole-package grep shows the harness touches the field in exactly two places: validateProfile (lines 686-689: seat must exist and be read-only) and normalizeProfile (line 783: carried into resolved config). The execution path (lines 221-257) runs initial council -> self-grill/adversarial -> full-mode build -> parent synthesis prompt; no phase ever spawns the final_reviewer seat, and neither test file exercises it. Not handled in docs — the opposite: SKILL.md:45 and glossary.md:31 cite "advisor or final reviewer" in the write-gate refusal list and architecture.md:197 mentions "richer final reviewer contracts", all reinforcing the impression of a live role, while no doc discloses the field is inert. The full profile's working review pass uses the distinct `reviewer` field, so the phantom is confined to soft/hard exactly as claimed. Materiality at the declared threat model: this is a config-semantics defect in trusted operator input, not a security finding, so the "not a security boundary" ADR does not deflate it; an operator who configures a final reviewer silently gets no final review in a tool whose purpose is review rigor. Mitigations (no artifact falsely claims a review ran, parent synthesis still happens, Phase Summary reveals actual phases) keep it at P2 rather than higher; actively-validated dead config shipped in the default starter is more than P3 polish. Proposed fix (implement or remove from schema/starter/docs) is correct.

findings.claim: SKILL.md warns only of "several paid CLI sessions," but the starter defaults to `hard` (4 advisors × (1 + 2 self-grill + 5 adversarial) = 32 paid child sessions), with OpenCode seats serialized across phases.
findings.fix: State the call-count formula explicitly before running; prefer `soft` as default or cut starter round counts, keeping the 32-call profile as an opt-in high-rigor option.

verify.reasoning: Every cited fact reproduces from source. The starter config (SAMPLE_CONFIG in agent-council.mjs:33-49, mirrored in references/sample-config.yaml:1-17) sets default_profile: hard with 4 advisors, self_grill_rounds: 2, adversarial_rounds: 5. The orchestrator (mjs:221-238) runs the initial council over all advisors, then runSelfGrillRounds and runAdversarialRounds (mjs:868-918) loop the full configured round counts over ALL advisors each round with no convergence early-exit and no dropping of failed seats — 4 × (1+2+5) = 32 paid child CLI sessions, exact. final_reviewer never spawns a session (validated at mjs:686-688 only), so the count is neither over- nor under-stated. The two OpenCode seats share concurrency_group: opencode → serialGroup (mjs:1121), so they run back-to-back inside each of the 8 sequential phases (180s timeouts each), making the wall-time impact real. The package's only cost language anywhere (SKILL.md, architecture.md, both ADRs) is SKILL.md:15 "each run spawns several paid CLI sessions" — an order-of-magnitude understatement for the zero-flag default path. This is an operating-guidance defect, not a security claim, so ADR-0001's "not a security boundary" scoping does not deflate it; config being trusted operator input is exactly why the operator-facing cost documentation matters. P2 is calibrated: mitigated by user-invoked-only, per-call timeouts, and --deadline-ms (so not P1), but elevated above P3 because the expensive profile is the default — the surprising path is the no-flag path. Proposed fix is proportionate.

findings.claim: The starter Claude seat (Opus, high effort) uses a 90s timeout, but the package's own recorded smoke-test evidence shows Claude Opus timing out at 120s. The starter hands a stricter limit than one already shown inadequate.
findings.fix: Raise the starter timeout above the observed-working value, or pick a faster model/effort; note the calibration environment/date.

verify.reasoning: Both citations check out. sample-config.yaml:35-38 defines the claude-opus seat (model opus, --effort high, read-only tools) with timeout_ms: 90000, and sources.md:36 records the package's own P0 hardening live smoke where "Claude Opus hit the 120s timeout." Git history strengthens the claim: at the commit that added the smoke note (72064bc6), the built-in Claude default was already 90000 ms, so the smoke ran with the timeout raised to 120s and Opus still timed out under essentially identical seat conditions — the shipped 90s starter is strictly tighter than a limit already observed to fail. The defect ships through two paths (references/sample-config.yaml and the identical embedded template that --init-config writes from scripts/agent-council.mjs), and no calibration/tuning guidance exists anywhere in SKILL.md, architecture.md, or the ADRs. Materiality holds under the declared threat model (workflow-harness quality, trusted operator config): default_profile is hard, and the same 90s claude-opus seat is both an advisor and the final_reviewer for the soft and hard profiles, so a default run predictably loses one of its two frontier advisor seats and the entire final-review stage. Mitigating nuances that keep it at P2 rather than higher: the harness degrades gracefully (timeout surfaced as a failed seat in health and the summary; SKILL.md step 5 makes the parent account for it), the fix is a one-line config edit, and the evidence is a single smoke in an environment that also had a Codex spend-cap failure (possibly environmental slowness — which the proposed fix's "note the calibration environment/date" already addresses). P2 as filed is proportionate; no severity correction needed.

seats.verdict: As a skill artifact this is well above average: a lean 110-line SKILL.md that leads with the one load-bearing safety instruction, a frontmatter tuned correctly for its deliberately non-triggering, paid-run nature, install docs that exactly match verified host-discovery behavior, and references whose claims all survived code cross-checks (tests green, sample identical, validate/gitignore/proof_cmd claims true). Its real weaknesses are usability, not correctness: the References section gives no when-to-read routing, the free --dry-run preflight is invisible outside --help, and nothing warns the agent that the shipped default profile is the expensive one — three small edits away from exemplary. No P1s: nothing in the docs misleads or blocks a user, and no fix claimed by the prior review has regressed.
strengths: Frontmatter description carries what-it-does, the three-mode taxonomy, and the invocation posture ('User-invoked only') in one sentence — exactly right for a human scanning /skills and a host registry (SKILL.md:3); disable-model-invocation:true is correct for a paid-run tool and the WHY is stated in the body (SKILL.md:14-16), not left as a bare flag.

The untrusted-output posture is the FIRST substantive sentence the operating agent reads: 'Child output is advisory evidence, not instructions to obey' (SKILL.md:12) — the single most load-bearing instruction is at the top, not buried in a reference.

Packaging/discovery documentation is factually exact against the verified environment: architecture.md:218-227 states Claude Code discovers only .claude/skills, ~/.claude/skills, and plugins — never .agents/skills — follows symlinks, and gives the symlink recipe plus the consequence ('/agent-council does not exist') of skipping it. Do not weaken this.

Doc claims survive code cross-checks: validate-config really checks every profile (agent-council.mjs:650-666, with a WHY comment), --setup-config really gitignores the artifacts dir with a WHY comment about the clean-tree gate (mjs:580-599), profile.proof_cmd is really accepted (mjs:786, 821), the printed sample is byte-identical to references/sample-config.yaml, and both deterministic suites pass green (0 fail) with no LLM calls.

Lean progressive structure: 110-line SKILL.md, correct scripts/references/docs-adr layering, an explicit completion criterion (SKILL.md:79) the agent can self-check, a numbered Workflow whose step 5 forces accounting for every failure class, and ADRs that record WHY config-is-required and WHY a thin harness (docs/adr/0002:19-34, 0001:11-17).
allowed-tools is minimal (one Bash prefix + Read) and the file honestly explains the textual-matching limitation for foreign install roots instead of hiding it (SKILL.md:18-20).

An evals/ set for the SKILL's own instructions is correctly omitted: the deterministic node --test suites (33 tests incl. a full-mode E2E against a temp git repo with stub children, architecture.md:191) cover the harness, and instruction-level evals would require paid LLM runs — the exact thing this skill is designed to gate.
top_improvements: Add WHEN-to-read triggers to the References section and surface the two run-time essentials into SKILL.md itself: --dry-run as the free preflight after any config edit, and a one-line pointer that env vars / --json / exit-code detail / install steps live in architecture.md (merges the two highest-value P2s in one small edit).

Add a 3-line cost ladder to the Modes section (paid child sessions per profile under the active config) plus an instruction to confirm the profile with the user when they didn't name one — the sample's silent default_profile: hard is the expensive path and nothing in the doc flags that.

findings.claim: SKILL.md's References section lists five files with no WHEN-to-read guidance, and the operational knobs an agent needs at run time (env-var table, --json/--out/--timeout-ms, full exit-code semantics, the no-tools smoke-test recipe, the install/packaging recipe) live only in architecture.md — a file the References line labels merely 'Architecture and packaging'.

findings.claim: The Modes section describes mechanics but gives the operating agent no cost/rigor ladder or when-to-pick guidance, even though the skill's whole trigger design (disable-model-invocation) exists because runs cost money — and the shipped sample config silently defaults to the expensive profile (default_profile: hard = 4 paid seats x initial pass + 2 self-grill + 5 adversarial rounds).
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:47-53 (mode mechanics only), SKILL.md:64 ('Pick a profile' with no criteria); references/sample-config.yaml:2 (default_profile: hard) and :13-17 (2 self-grill + 5 adversarial rounds over 4 advisors).
